title: Derivation of Fokker-Planck equation and its entropy production
authors: Tânia Tomé, Mário J. de Oliveira
abstract: We derive the Fokker-Planck equation and its entropy production from the master equation. To this end we consider a discrete space of states where the master equation is defined and appropriate transition rates are introduced. A transition rate has two parts, one of which is the ordinary term proportional to the inverse of the spacing and the other is inversely proportional to the square of the spacing corresponding to the variance of the independent stochastic variable. In the continuous space limit, we obtain the Fokker-Planck as well as the rate of entropy production and the flux of entropy. We also consider the case where the space of states is the phase space and discuss the equations appropriate for systems in contact with several heat reservoirs and for isolated systems.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework to derive the Fokker-Planck equation from a discrete master equation by taking the continuum limit. It rigorously calculates the rate of entropy production and entropy flux for systems coupled to heat reservoirs or isolated systems. This provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium dynamics in statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper derives the Fokker-Planck equation and rigorously calculates the associated rate of entropy production from the underlying master equation.
main_result: The derivation successfully yields the Fokker-Planck equation and provides explicit, thermodynamically consistent formulas for the entropy production rate ($P$) and entropy flux ($\Psi$).
method: The core method involves taking the continuous space limit ($\epsilon 	o 0$) of a discrete master equation, allowing the transition from stochastic jump processes to continuous diffusion equations.
model_or_system: The analysis models general stochastic motion, applicable to systems interacting with multiple heat reservoirs or isolated systems, using a state space $x$ (generalized to phase space).
key_observables: Probability density $ho(x)$, Entropy $S$, Entropy Production $P$, and Entropy Flux $\Psi$.
important_parameters: The small parameter $\epsilon$ (related to the discretization spacing), temperature $T_i$, and the system Hamiltonian $H$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the assumption that the time evolution of entropy can be decomposed as $dS/dt = P - \Psi$, and that certain integrated parts vanish during the limit process.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the master equation for discrete states, then deriving the continuous Fokker-Planck equation in the limit $\epsilon 	o 0$. It subsequently analyzes the entropy balance, deriving expressions for $P$ and $\Psi$ for coupled systems and isolated systems, confirming thermodynamic consistency.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, general framework for deriving non-equilibrium statistical mechanics equations (like the Fokker-Planck equation) directly from microscopic jump processes, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems and thermalization dynamics.
